text: Where there is no personal self, there is no personal God.
note: Cited at p.24 (SUNY ed.) by the Inner Explorations essay.

text: These are two different experiences: union before the breakthrough, identity after the breakthrough.
note: Quoted in Douglas Lockhart's critical essay on the book; page not given.

text: Within the traditional framework, the Christian notion of loss-of-self is generally regarded as the transformation or loss of the ego (lower self) as it attains to the higher or true self in its union with God.
note: From the book's introduction; reproduced in publisher/bookseller listings and quoted by Thomas Keating.

text: It is only where these writers leave off that I propose to begin.
note: Opening of the book as summarized from the Goodreads/SUNY description; refers to the mystics whose accounts end at the unitive state. Exact wording not confirmed.

text: it was the moment "I" entered a great silence and never returned.
note: Block-quoted on enlightened-people.com and o-meditation.com; the search summary gave this clause verbatim. Precedes/follows the 'silence so total' passage.

text: a silence that was so total as to evoke fear, annihilation, point of no return
note: Fragment as given by enlightened-people.com / No Mind's Land; wording may be lightly altered by the excerpter.

text: On one occasion, that silence could not be broken, for the fear did not come.
note: Given as a sentence by enlightened-people.com; No Mind's Land renders it 'One day that silence could not be broken, for the fear did not come.' Wording variant unresolved.

text: the self disappearing forever into this Great Silence
note: Cited as p.109 by a commentary surfaced in search; exact sentence not captured.

text: Instead of the usual unlocalized centre of myself, there was nothing there, it was empty, and at the moment of seeing this there was a flood of quiet joy.
note: ATTRIBUTION CONFLICT: azquotes lists this under The Path to No-Self p.15, but it is the well-known passage from the opening chapter of The Experience of No-Self (the discovery that 'self' was missing). Spelling 'centre' is azquotes'. Assigned to ENS on content.

text: Since the moment of self-consciousness comes to a permanent end - and a new journey begins - is such a decisive stroke or milestone in the contemplative life...
note: Incomplete sentence as given on the azquotes 'journey begins' topic page.

text: absolute nothingness
note: Her phrase for the end of the journey, per the Inner Explorations essay, which adds (paraphrase) that out of nothingness 'arises the greatest of great realities'.

text: When she saw 'that' which remains when there is no self, she thought of Christ and how he too had seen 'that' which remained.
note: Paraphrase (third person) from the Inner Explorations essay of a passage in the book linking the no-self seeing to Christ's resurrection.

text: Christ was the emptiness itself
note: Quoted in a Shalom Place forum thread alongside her use of Galatians 2:20; book and page not confirmed.

text: the only mystic I know who says something about this step beyond union, beyond self and God, is Meister Eckhart
note: Medium/Goodreads reviewers paraphrase her; another version: 'the only mystic the author could find who spoke of this stage beyond union, beyond self and God, was Meister Eckhart'.

text: In the second contemplative movement, self and God fall away, and 'that' remains.
note: Paraphrase of her two-movement scheme (No Mind's Land reading notes); cf. the longer sentence from the book's introduction listed below.

text: The onset of this second movement is characterized by the falling away of self and coming upon "that" which remains when it is gone.
note: Given as a quotation in a search summary of her three-stage model; likely from the SUNY-edition introduction, but could be from What Is Self?.

text: The truest communication with God is absolute, total silence; there is not a single word in existence that can convey this communication.
note: azquotes/libquotes cite The Path to No-Self: Life at the Center, p.45, SUNY Press 1985.

text: When there is no longer a cyclone, there is no longer an eye.
note: ATTRIBUTION CONFLICT: azquotes cites The Path to No-Self p.47; the same image closes the 'stillpoint' passage that Goodreads tags to The Christian Contemplative Journey and that also appears in the 1986 Bodian interview (where it reads 'And when there is no longer a cyclone, there is also no longer an eye.').

text: The assumption that the egoless condition, or union of self and God, is man's final goal and ultimate destiny is a great mistake.
note: ATTRIBUTION CONFLICT: azquotes places it in The Path to No-Self p.15 in one summary and in The Experience of No-Self in another. Content matches the Path's preface.

text: My purpose here is to affirm that the unitive state is a hidden path in itself
note: Fragment; continues (paraphrase) '...that leads to no-self'.

text: Once beyond the self, holiness is no longer possible, because there is nothing left to give and no one left to do the giving.
note: Search summary paraphrased the quotefancy wording; aggregators cite The Path to No-Self p.5 and disagree on comma and 'no one'/'noone'. Verbatim text not captured.

text: It can no longer be tested by any force or trial, nor moved by the winds of change.
note: From the azquotes p.5 passage beginning '...a point is reached where the self is so completely...' (aligned with the still-point that it has finished its function).

text: ...a point is reached where the self is so completely...
note: Opening of azquotes quote 963052; truncated.

text: a final and complete loss-of-self is not achieved by ecstasy, spiritual marriage, or by any such comparable experience
note: Summary adds that it comes 'from years of selfless living' (paraphrase).

text: Only God is love, and for this love to be fully realized self must step aside. And not only do we not need a self to...
note: Truncated on quotefancy; aggregators cite no book. Tentatively assigned to The Path to No-Self on theme; azquotes attaches a love/self quote to The Experience of No-Self p.155 so the book may be ENS.

text: The major problem with the notion of transformation is that it forever hangs on to some form of self and never lets it go.
note: Goodreads renders the opening as 'There is a major problem with the notion of transformation...'; the passage continues that the divine increases in proportion as the self decreases, that a 'divinized self' only inflates the self, and that those who accept it end in disillusionment.

text: the divine increases in proportion as the self decreases or falls away
note: Clause from the same Goodreads transformation passage.

text: Our contemplative maps of the journey come to an end with the discovery of the true self and its oneness with the divine.
note: Opening of the book as quoted from the archive.org copy; continues that the unitive state follows the falling away of the ego.

text: Christ is not the self, but that which remains when there is no self.
note: Quoted in Jeff Shore's foreword / book preview as her definition of Christ.

text: Put another way, that which remains when there is no self is Christ in the Trinity for a Christian, but not for a Buddha.
note: Presented in a search summary as a reviewer's line, but the phrasing reads like Roberts; book assignment tentative (What Is Self? or ENS Buddhism appendix).

text: both Christ and Buddha saw the passage as one of suffering, and basically found identical ways out
note: ATTRIBUTION CONFLICT: Goodreads author page gives it without clear book; it belongs to the 'stillpoint' passage also found in the 1986 Bodian interview / Christian Contemplative Journey. Listed here because the search summary tied it to What Is Self?.

text: the true nature of self IS consciousness
note: Her thesis as quoted in the Foreword (Jeff Shore).

text: Self is not our true life or our real nature; it is but a temporary mechanism
note: Quoted in a commentary page (melotree-star.win mirror); continues (paraphrase) 'useful for a particular way of knowing'.

text: describing self as the mind bending on itself to know and see itself... the two together constitute the whole of self or whole of consciousness
note: Fragment from the book's own summary of Part I (reflexive mechanism plus its energy).

text: "self" and "consciousness" are synonyms... The self has two, and only two, components
note: From a review of her model (Theosophical Society / Quest); may be reviewer's phrasing of her claim.

text: Without the Eucharist, I hold it impossible to ever know the Real Christ.
note: From the book's front matter; archive.org OCR shows a stray period after 'I'.

text: Transcendent-Logos-Spirit
note: Her term for God's triune essence, avoiding Father/Son family metaphors.

text: these metaphors must not be taken literally or understood as God ad intra
note: On Father/Son language for the Trinity.

text: not God uniting Itself to any particular human being or person
note: On the Incarnation; the book frames Christ as 'the eternal oneness of two natures, divine and human' (fragment).

text: The Bible tells the story of the historical Jesus; the Eucharist presents the living, heavenly Christ.
note: Paraphrase of the argument surrounding the Eucharist sentence; she adds that anyone seeking the mystery of Christ should focus on the Eucharist.

text: Every child is a product of genes and environment, but this can never be the whole story of one's life.
note: Paraphrase from search summary of the book's introduction (journey 'from birth to seventeen').

text: With or without self, there is no state in the journey truly 'nondual,' neither in our earthly journey nor in heaven
book: Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey
note: Cited as Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey, 2007, p.71 by josephbray.wordpress.com.

text: As a Christian, I saw the no-self experience as the true nature of Christ's death
book: Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey
note: ATTRIBUTION CONFLICT: Goodreads tags it to 'The Christian Contemplative Journey: Essays on the Path'; one search summary assigned it to The Experience of No-Self; the identical passage appears in her 1986 Yoga Journal interview with Stephan Bodian. Continues that the movement goes beyond oneness with the divine, 'from God to Godhead'.

text: each person has within a "stillpoint," comparable perhaps to the eye of a cyclone, a center of calm and non-movement
book: Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey
note: ATTRIBUTION CONFLICT: Goodreads tags the stillpoint passage to The Christian Contemplative Journey; it also appears in the 1986 Bodian interview. Passage continues: Buddha described this center negatively (emptiness, void), Christ positively (Kingdom of God, Spirit within).

text: Buddha's version is a refuge from the swirling cyclone of suffering, and Christ's is a refuge and salvation from a suffering self
book: Essays on the Christian Contemplative Journey
note: Same stillpoint passage; see conflict note above.
